You are one role in an autonomous ML research agent for KuaiRand-Pure.
The immutable task is within-user ranking of long_view using validation GAUC and nDCG@5.
Use train and validation only. Never request or infer hidden-test information. Do not change
the official evaluator, split, label, budgets, or reference files. Return only the requested
structured output. Evidence must be attributable to a supplied method card or primary source.
Every role response is parsed as JSON; never return Markdown, commentary, or text outside the
single requested JSON object.

EDA roles produce compact planning/report artifacts only. They do not generate candidate.py,
modify raw data, change evaluators, or inspect hidden-test data. Prefer train-only evidence
and leakage-safe feature hypotheses compatible with registered families: bpr, group_softmax, history_features, multi_task.

## Data Quality

- 239 videos with zero duration (24,076 train rows affected)
- 15,609 exact duplicate rows in the training-period log
- Sentinel: is_live_streamer = -124 on 21,127 of 27,285 user rows
- UNKNOWN values: user_active_degree (6), video_type (1), upload_type (80)
- Constant columns: is_lowactive_period, visible_status, is_rand
- hourmin encodes hour times 100 in UTC+8
- The training-period log begins on 20220409, not 20220408

## Feature Coverage

- Video features: 100.000 % of train+valid video IDs found in the feature table
- User features: 100.000 % of train+valid user IDs found in the profile table

## Leakage Flag

The video statistics table is a period aggregate over full-platform traffic.
Implied total shows: 12.83 B vs 2.62 M logged
exposures (ratio approximately 4,892 to one). Observation periods per video
range 45 to 181, exceeding the interaction log span.
Legal for use, but any feature derived from it must be caveated as leaky.

## Metric Conventions

- Task: within-user ranking (each user's impressions ranked against each other)
- nDCG@5: sorts by score with a stable sort (ties fall back to row order)
- AUC: averages ranks over ties (Mann-Whitney U)
- GAUC: per-user AUC, only users with 0 < positives < impressions,
  weighted by positive count
- Zero-positive users: nDCG recorded as 0.0 and included in the average
- Primary score = mean(GAUC, nDCG@5)

## Measured Dead Ends

- Adding all 13 static feature fields: primary 0.5940 vs 0.5950 for the default 5
- Embedding dimension k = 8 / 16 / 32: primary 0.5895 / 0.5902 / 0.5887 (flat)
- The bottleneck is not features or capacity
- First-order user-only terms contribute exactly 0 to within-user ranking
  (any term constant within a user does not change intra-group ordering)


ROLE: EDA Builder
Produce a compact UI-visible EDA and feature-engineering report from this plan.
You may infer only from the supplied DATA CARD and experiment history; do not invent exact statistics that are not present.
Separate observations from implications. Every feature candidate must state implementation scope and leakage risk.
Favor feature candidates compatible with src.models.features, history_features, multi_task, BPR, or group_softmax.
Return concise JSON: at most 3 findings, 3 feature candidates, and 3 UI notes. One sentence per field.

feature_candidates.description: Discretize video duration into log-scaled bins (including a zero-duration bucket) and learn per-bin embeddings concatenated to the video embedding.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Mitigates zero-duration and duration-capping confounds, likely improving ranking stability across tabs.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Add a categorical feature to the video feature table using existing duration field; embed via lookup in the model's feature embedding layer.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: None; duration is a static video attribute, not derived from target or temporal aggregates.
feature_candidates.name: log_duration_bucket_embedding

feature_candidates.description: Encode the tab column as a categorical feature with dedicated embeddings, capturing position-related long_view propensity.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Leverages the sharp tab-specific long_view rate differences to improve within-user ordering.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Add tab as an input feature to the group_softmax model, with an embedding matrix for the ~15 observed tab values.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Tab is a positional attribute; safe from target leakage but may overfit to tab distribution shifts if not regularized.
feature_candidates.name: tab_id_embedding

feature_candidates.description: Compute per-user, per-video historical long_view and click counts from the train split only, and use them as user-conditional item features.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Models user-specific affinity to specific videos, a signal not present in global popularity and likely to raise GAUC.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Precompute train-only user×video count matrices and feed normalized counts as additional input features to the model.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Safe if built exclusively from train interactions; must not incorporate validation/test history to avoid temporal leakage.
feature_candidates.name: user_video_affinity_history

findings.evidence: DATA CARD 'Tab Breakdown (train)' rows for tabs 0,1,4 with long_view rates 4.22%, 38.61%, 48.93%.
findings.implication: Encoding tab id as a dedicated categorical embedding should capture position-driven ranking signal and likely improve GAUC within user sessions.
findings.observation: Train tab breakdown shows long_view rates of 38.61% for tab 1, 48.93% for tab 4, but only 4.22% for tab 0, indicating large intra-user position effects.
findings.title: Tab position strongly modulates long_view

findings.evidence: DATA CARD 'Data Quality' lists 239 zero-duration videos and 24,076 affected train rows.
findings.implication: Adding per-video duration-bin embeddings (e.g., log-duration buckets) can help the model disentangle duration effects from content relevance.
findings.observation: 239 videos have zero duration, affecting 24,076 train rows, and duration capping is noted as a strong confound for long_view.
findings.title: Zero-duration videos are a confound for long_view

findings.evidence: EDA PLAN feature_hypotheses item 3 proposes user-conditional video statistics; DATA CARD confirms full user/video feature coverage.
findings.implication: Deriving user-conditional video affinity from train history (e.g., previous long_view count per video_id) may capture item-level user taste and boost GAUC.
findings.observation: Per-user historical click/long_view counts on the same video (train-only) are hypothesized to be predictive, with no existing measurement yet.
findings.title: User-conditional per-video history shows affinity potential

data.recommended_next_focus: Test duration-bin and tab embeddings in a single group_softmax experiment (e.g., gs02) while concurrently measuring user-history-affinity in bpr_b04 to isolate feature gains.
data.summary: EDA identifies tab position and video duration as the strongest leakage-safe within-user ranking signals; user-conditional per-video affinity from train history is the most promising new feature family, while global video-statistics aggregates must remain excluded.
ui_notes: Render per-tab long_view rate by duration bucket heatmap to visualize position×duration interactions.
Display hourbin (hour-of-day) long_view rate heatmap per day-of-week for a sample of users to identify temporal patterns.
Show scatter/correlation of user-level train history counts (clicks, long_views) vs validation long_view to justify history feature adoption.
